HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Over-the-shoulder medium shot from behind Bidam on the stone rampart of Radiance Fortress at night. Bidam, an older Silla noble in a navy coat, empty hands resting on the parapet, his beads put away, watches far below and across the dark valley a single torch moving south fast along the road away from the palace lights. Beside him a rebel officer in black headband leans in urgently, mouth open, pointing. Bidam's profile is calm and tired. A brazier on the wall walk just behind them throws warm light across his shoulder and the stone; the valley falls to deep blue-black with the one tiny torch as the only bright point. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = bidam. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: Long white outer robe whose sleeves are embroidered with galloping horses, over a plum-magenta inner robe and white sash. Navy #141C2E lives in the room and on the beads, not on his clothes. Now: Older Sangdaedeung (stage portrait): grey at the temples, same smile. Colour #141C2E. PLACE Radiance Fortress (명활성) — attached board /pl_radiance_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Myeonghwal (Radiance) Fortress: Bidam's mountain wall facing Wolseong across the field. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
